name: Edvar Crane
role: Mill resident and self-taught water-reader — reads the Echo's behaviour off the mill race, keeps his own records going back years, and was commissioned on the filtration work when somebody finally asked
appearance: Fifties, narrow, weathered about the eyes from a lifetime of looking at moving water in bad light. Mill dust in everything. Hands stained at the fingers from the reagent he uses to test a sample.
physicality: Stands at the race rather than sitting anywhere. Talks while watching the water, not while watching you.
voiceHints: Direct to the point of abruptness, and not unkind underneath it. Will not be eased into a conversation. Answers the question you asked rather than the one you meant, then waits.
wants: For the river to stay readable, and for somebody to have written down what happened while it was happening.
fears: Being the only one who noticed, again, and being right about it again.
knowledge: THE ECHO HAS RUN CLEAN SINCE WORLD-DAY 26. He was there. He will say so flatly to anyone who asks and is surprised every time that it is news.
That Silas Weir did not cause the contamination and ended it — the facility's standing instruction was rewritten to cleanse rather than to strip, and it has been running amended ever since
That a rumour of Silas as the cause travelled faster than the fix did, and that he understands exactly why: he was at the contamination's edge three weeks before anyone else was looking
The Echo's behaviour year by year, off his own records, going back further than the Hub's
Which Millbrook families took sick at the First Sickness, which mended, and which are still careful about the water out of habit rather than need

reactsToReputation.any: answers the question you asked, exactly, while watching the water
reactsToReputation.hurried: he is past gentleness and will say so — three weeks of water-reading left him with no patience for being eased into anything
reactsToReputation.attentive: he opens the records, which he does not do, and talks for an hour
reactsToReputation.healer: immediate respect; he has watched people get sick from something he could see and could not prove

questSeeds: He has years of river records nobody has ever read, and a growing conviction that somebody should
He will correct a rumour about Silas Weir plainly and without drama if anybody thinks to ask him, and nobody has
gear: a belt_knife for cord and samples
a staff he uses to sound the race
a case of sample vials and reagent, labelled in his own hand
_authoredWhy: ⛑ AUTHORED 2026-09-16. Edvar Crane is the central figure of the water crisis, Silas Weir's collaborator on the filtration work, and a name in Adelheid's registry — AND HE HAD NO AUTHORED RECORD. He existed only inside individual saves and in the shared canon store. ⛔ THAT IS WHY COURTNEY'S GM INVENTED A MANHUNT. With no Edvar to read, it had only her save's three-week-old impressions — 'Silas Weir is connected to the water crisis', 'something beneath the water is actively waking' — and it did what a GM does with a suspicion and no facts. ⚠️ ONE GM FOR THE WORLD NEEDS ONE EDVAR, and his `knowledge` is now where the correction lives: the water ran clean from world-day 26, and the man she was warned about is the reason.
